name: How do you estimate apartment construction cost from square footage?

mainEntity.name: What is the best way to turn square footage into a realistic apartment building budget in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: What is the best way to turn square footage into a realistic apartment building budget in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Square footage is useful for early budgeting, but it cannot tell the full story for apartment construction in Los Angeles. A more realistic estimate starts with building type, unit count, parking solution, site conditions, and finish level, then layers in soft costs and contingency. Two projects with the same square footage can have very different costs if one needs subterranean parking, complicated utilities, or a more expensive structural system. A better budgeting method is to estimate by unit count and by building component. That means separately considering shell, MEP systems, parking, finishes, site work, and professional fees. This approach is especially important in Los Angeles because code and site constraints can create expensive surprises. If the goal is investment analysis, the estimate should also reflect carrying costs and the likely approval timeline. Square footage alone is too blunt to determine whether a project will be feasible.
